Bootstrap rank instability of the logistic propensity model

Source: R/bootstrap_rank_instability.R
bootstrap_rank_instability.Rd

Descriptive. The sampling noise of the analyst's logistic model: logistic regression with the formula as written (including any interactions or transformations) is refitted on bootstrap_samples nonparametric bootstrap samples of all patients, the original patients are ranked by each refit's logit (percentile rank rank(logit, ties = "average") / n, on a 0 to 1 scale), and for each patient the standard deviation of the rank over the refits is taken. The study-level value is the mean over treated patients. A bootstrap sample with fewer than 10 treated or 10 untreated patients is skipped (the rule of match_each_model()).

Usage

bootstrap_rank_instability(
  x,
  data = NULL,
  bootstrap_samples = 20,
  cores = 1,
  seed = 1,
  clip_bootstrap = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'bootstrap_rank_instability'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

x

One of: a propensity_sensitivity object or a match_set from match_each_model() (the stored bootstrap ranks are used, nothing is refitted); a matchit object (its formula is used); or a two-sided formula such as treat ~ x1 + x2.

data

The data frame. Required with a formula; with a matchit object it is looked up from the object's call when NULL. Not used for stored ranks.

bootstrap_samples

Number of bootstrap refits (default 20). Not used for stored ranks.

cores

Number of cores (default 1). Not used for stored ranks.

seed

Integer seed from which every other seed is derived; the same seed gives the bootstrap samples of match_each_model(). Not used for stored ranks.

clip_bootstrap

FALSE (default) or TRUE: clip the refits' scores to [0.001, 0.999], the default clip of fit_propensity_models(). Not used for stored ranks.

...

Not used.

Value

An object of class "bootstrap_rank_instability": a list with patients (one row per patient: id, treated, rank_instability), summary (mean_treated, samples_used, samples_requested, samples_skipped) and settings. mean_treated is NA when fewer than two bootstrap samples are usable.

Details

It uses the covariates and the treatment only, no outcome. Report it next to rank disagreement: it shows how much the logistic model's ranks move from sampling alone. It describes the analyst's logistic model only, whatever distance the matchit object used. The refits' scores are not clipped by default, unlike the cross-fitted scores (see clip_bootstrap). These diagnostics have been studied in the author's simulations and benchmark analyses; a methods paper is in preparation. No peer-reviewed evaluation exists yet.

Examples

data("lalonde", package = "MatchIt")
instability <- bootstrap_rank_instability(
  treat ~ age + educ + race + married + nodegree + re74 + re75,
  data = lalonde, bootstrap_samples = 5
)
instability
#> Bootstrap rank instability of the logistic model (mean over treated): 0.03605
#> SD of the percentile rank over 5 bootstrap refits
instability$summary$mean_treated
#> [1] 0.0360503
